title: Virtues of Salawat on Friday
summary: The hadith emphasizes the virtues of sending blessings on Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), especially on Fridays, with promises of divine mercy.
translation: Muslims should make it a point to frequently send Salawat (blessings) on Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) on Fridays. While there are general virtues of sending Salawat, sending them more abundantly on Fridays holds even more virtue. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), as narrated by Anas (RA), said, 'Send blessings upon me in abundance on Friday and on Friday night, for whoever sends one Salawat upon me, Allah will send ten mercies upon them.' Engaging in studying the hadith of the Prophet (PBUH) and sending Salawat as decreed in the Quran, where Allah commands, "Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, ask [Allah to confer] blessing upon him and ask [Allah to grant him] peace." When the companions learned of this verse, they asked the Prophet (PBUH) for the method of sending Salawat, and he taught them the Salat al-Ibrahimiyya, which is read in Salah. Sending Salawat is a right of the Prophet (PBUH) upon the believers; thus, it is obligatory to recite it at least once in a lifetime. Reciting Salawat more frequently, even multiple times in a single gathering, signifies greater virtue and faith. It testifies to the love for the Prophet (PBUH). The current circumstances demand that we revive the love for the Prophet (PBUH) in our hearts and frequently send him our Salawat and peace. Doing so brings great mercy upon our homes and families. Allah has promised multiple blessings and mercies for one instance of Salawat, even up to seventy in some narrations. There are many significant rewards and benefits for believers who engage in this practice. Narrated in Tirmidhi and Mishkat, the Prophet (PBUH) expressed joy when Jibreel (AS) informed him that Allah sends ten mercies for each Salawat and ten peace for each Salam. The hadith reinforces that those who often send Salawat on the Prophet (PBUH) will be closest to him on the Day of Judgment. Angels on earth convey the Salawat from his followers, ensuring the continuous delivery of these blessings to the Prophet (PBUH). Therefore, we should persistently send Salawat on the Prophet (PBUH) and strive to please him and Allah, creating a favorable outcome for ourselves and our families.
